text: Ordinal arithmetic is not commutative. Which statement correctly reflects this, where ω is the least infinite ordinal?
explanation: Prepending one element to a copy of ℕ yields an order isomorphic to ℕ, so 1 + ω = ω; appending one element after all of ℕ yields a strictly longer well-order, so ω + 1 > ω. Thus 1 + ω ≠ ω + 1 — ordinal addition is non-commutative. Option A denies the non-commutativity; options C and D reverse which sum grows.
